question: Does the same Zhao Wanli 1951 donation passage used in Batch 12HF supply a distinct Qu-family donation count and named-member anchor, and how should its 62-title figure relate to the 52-title February-1950 diary report?
answer: Yes. Xiao Ling's 2026 scholarly article reproduces the relevant Zhao Wanli passage through 《赵万里文集：第一卷》 p.197. In the same 1951 text that names Ding Huikang's six-title donation, Zhao states that, among rare books sent to Beijing Library through the Cultural Relics Bureau in the preceding roughly two years, Qu Jicang, Qu Fengqi and Qu Xuchu donated a Song-printed 《春秋左传注疏》 and other books totaling 62 titles. This creates a later publication-text quotation bridge for a 62-title Qu-family donation summary and one explicitly named member. It does not directly collate the 1951 original issue or the 2011 p.197 page. The 62 count differs from Song Yunbin's public excerpt of the 1950-02-11 diary report of Zhao Wanli, which says 52 titles were donated. The ten-title arithmetic difference is not evidence of a discrete later ten-title donation: publication date layer, cumulative scope, cataloging/counting convention, reporting revision or additional transfers may explain the difference. Gu Tinglong's mediated Jan-6 42-title report remains another unresolved comparator. No count normalization is authorized.
